newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates broadly stable, trade peters out.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates broadly stable, trade peters out.

text.p: Dutch money market rates were virtually unmoved from Tuesday's levels on Wednesday and dealers said the market seriously lacked impetus.
Call rates eased slightly, with overnight money changing hands between 3.18 and 3.25 percent, down from Tuesday's 3.25 to 3.31 percent.
"On the offer side, quotations went down somewhat this morning and the bid side followed, but without much trade actually being done," one dealer said.
Dealers said trade in Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs) was probably negligible, as the Finance Ministry Agency's indicative prices were far out of line with market levels.
Paper maturing in July was set at 3.13 percent, DTCs maturing in August at 3.15 percent and those in December 3.20 percent, all unchanged from Tuesday.
"These prices are simply saying 'stay-away', so I don't think anything has been done," another dealer said.
"If you see a good bank setting six months deposits at 3.28, you don't get into DTCs at these levels," he added.
Six month deposits were quoted around 3.24-3.32 percent.
Dealers expect the new special advances pact, to be announced on Thursday, to be set at an unchanged rate of 2.90 percent.
The guilder was steady against the mark at 112.53 per 100 marks.
